title: Tokenizer-atomizer CFG backend and streaming-safe tool-call framing
author: Marta Delgado
description:
Context: Structured-output decoding in the OpenAI-compat layer has repeatedly surfaced tokenizer boundary mismatches when combining CFG/grammar constraints with streaming and function/tool calling. These mismatches cause dropped tokens at chunk boundaries, broken JSON fragments for tool calls, and brittle fallbacks when a grammar node crosses tokenizer token edges. Motivation: Provide a lightweight, backwards-compatible shim for CFG-style backends that is aware of tokenizer atomization and streaming chunk boundaries so structured outputs (JSON, function calls) remain valid across streaming transport, and so grammar constraints do not spuriously reject valid continuations due to tokenization artifacts. This change introduces an intermediate 'token-atomizer' stage and a streaming framing policy for tool/function calls. Goals: 1) Prevent truncated JSON/function call fragments at stream flush boundaries 2) Keep latency and throughput impact minimal 3) Maintain compatibility with existing regex and legacy CFG backends (fallback unchanged) 4) Provide observability and a clear rollback path

What I changed (high-level): - Added a token-atomizer component in the constrained-decoder pipeline. The atomizer maps tokenizer tokens to 'atoms' that preserve join points used by CFG productions; it exposes safe-split boundaries for streaming flushes. - Modified CFG backend to operate over atoms rather than raw tokens for constraint checks. This keeps grammar matchers stable when tokenizer splits produce partial UTF-8/byte sequences. - Implemented a streaming-safe framing policy for OpenAI-compat tool/function calls: when the decoder emits a candidate that begins a tool call frame (e.g., "{"tool_call": ..."), the runtime delays flushes until the atomizer indicates a safe boundary or a short grace window expires. - Introduced a minimal compatibility adapter: if an upstream backend cannot use atomized tokens (legacy regex or third-party backends), the adapter translates atomic constraints into token-level checks and falls back to a conservative mode. - Added instrumentation: metrics for atomization collisions, framing backpressure events, and a histogram of added latency due to framing (for SLO analysis). - Tests: unit tests for atomizer boundary behavior, end-to-end streaming tests with simulated chunking over TCP and SSE, and fuzz tests that interleave UTF-8 multi-byte sequences with grammar productions.

review_comments: Jordan Wu: Can the atomizer be shared across multiple requests to avoid extra allocations? Response: we added a pooled atomizer instance with per-request scratch space; see commit 5b8a2d3.

Priya Nair: Are we confident the grace window won't mask generator failure modes? Response: yes — default is conservative (max 64 tokens), and we added telemetry to surface long grace windows; operator can set to 0 to disable.
Ethan Brooks: CI flake on streaming e2e in first run. Response: Reproduced locally; fixed race in flusher.go and re-ran CI.
release_notes: Introduce a tokenizer-aware atomizer and streaming-safe framing for constrained decoding; improves stability of structured outputs (JSON/function calls) across streaming transports. Backwards-compatible adapter included for legacy backends.
